meta.source: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet (selected values, rounded)
meta.notes: Core physical/orbital values are approximate and intended for educational UI display.

planets.name: Mercury
planets.summary: The smallest planet and closest to the Sun, with extreme day/night temperature swings.
planets.atmosphere: Extremely thin exosphere (oxygen, sodium, hydrogen, helium, potassium).
notableFacts: A solar day lasts about 176 Earth days.
Its surface is heavily cratered like Earth’s Moon.

planets.name: Venus
planets.summary: Earth-sized but shrouded in dense clouds, with a runaway greenhouse effect.
planets.atmosphere: Very dense carbon dioxide with sulfuric acid clouds.
notableFacts: Hottest planetary surface in the Solar System.

planets.name: Earth
planets.summary: The only known world with stable liquid water oceans and life.
notableFacts: About 71% of the surface is covered by water.
Plate tectonics helps regulate long-term climate.

planets.name: Mars
planets.summary: A cold desert planet with the largest volcano and canyon in the Solar System.
notableFacts: Home to Olympus Mons and Valles Marineris.
Evidence suggests ancient liquid water on its surface.

planets.name: Jupiter
planets.summary: The largest planet, with powerful storms and a deep atmosphere of hydrogen and helium.
notableFacts: The Great Red Spot is a centuries-old storm.
Its magnetic field is the strongest of any planet.

planets.name: Saturn
planets.summary: Known for its bright ring system made largely of ice particles.
notableFacts: Its average density is lower than water.
Rings are broad but extremely thin.

planets.name: Uranus
planets.summary: An ice giant that rotates on its side relative to its orbital plane.
notableFacts: Its sideways tilt likely comes from an ancient giant impact.
Methane in the atmosphere gives it a blue-green color.

planets.name: Neptune
planets.summary: A distant, dynamic world with supersonic winds and dark storm systems.
notableFacts: Fastest sustained winds measured on any planet.
Triton, its largest moon, orbits in retrograde.

planets.name: Pluto
planets.summary: A Kuiper Belt dwarf planet with nitrogen ice plains and a complex seasonal cycle.
planets.atmosphere: Thin, variable nitrogen atmosphere with methane and carbon monoxide.
notableFacts: Charon is large enough that Pluto-Charon is often described as a binary system.
First close-up images were captured by New Horizons in 2015.
